entries.falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2 million units for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Buyers keep ordering more accelerators than NVIDIA can build because memory and packaging limit output, so the order book grows faster than shipments.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to a cut in hyperscaler capital-spending plans, since four buyers drive most of the order book.
entries.statement: Datacenter GPU demand continues to outrun NVIDIA's ability to serve it.
entries.title: NVDA demand durability

entries.falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand and CoWoS lead times fall below 26 weeks before the end of 2027.
entries.mechanism: Every accelerator needs both stacked memory and advanced packaging, so whichever of the two is scarcer sets the ceiling on how many parts vendors can ship.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast new packaging and memory capacity actually comes online versus the 2027 order book.
entries.statement: Memory and advanced packaging are both capping how much merchant-GPU vendors can ship, with high-bandwidth memory sold out through 2027 and TSMC packaging booked out at 52 to 78 week lead times even as capacity climbs toward 130,000 wafers a month.
entries.title: Supply constraint binding

entries.falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.
entries.mechanism: Buyers who cannot get enough NVIDIA parts sign large AMD commitments, and those commitments turn into shipped racks once AMD's rack-scale system reaches production.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to AMD's share of scarce packaging output, which it must split between its server processors and its accelerators.
entries.statement: AMD converts its Instinct roadmap into material datacenter share.
entries.title: AMD credible second source

entries.falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Large cloud buyers move their steady inference work onto chips they design themselves, which takes growth away from the merchant accelerators they would otherwise buy.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether in-house chips stay captive to their owners or become rentable to outside customers.
entries.statement: Hyperscaler custom silicon meaningfully displaces merchant-GPU demand growth.
entries.title: Custom ASIC substitution

entries.falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for H100 or GB200 drops more than 20% within a quarter.
entries.mechanism: New capacity arrives more slowly than new workloads, so renters bid up the hourly rate instead of waiting for cheaper supply.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to a simultaneous multi-vendor supply wave landing while buyers pause new workloads.
entries.statement: GPU rental/spot price levels hold up despite added supply.
entries.title: Pricing power persistence

entries.falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within two quarters.
entries.mechanism: Licence rules and tariffs keep the largest single foreign market mostly closed, so demand that exists there cannot be billed.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether approved licences convert into actual shipments rather than staying on paper.
entries.statement: Export-control policy materially constrains addressable merchant-GPU demand.
entries.title: Export control exposure

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within two quarters.
entries.mechanism: The chip seller supplies the money and the rent guarantee that let thinly funded buyers place orders, so some reported demand is the seller's own credit coming back as revenue.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the backed clouds can pay from real customer rentals rather than from the guarantee.
entries.statement: NVIDIA's own revenue-sharing and credit-support financing increasingly underwrites its accelerator demand, coupling reported demand strength to NVIDIA-extended credit and adding circularity risk to buildout durability.
entries.title: Vendor-financed demand circularity

entries.falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.
entries.mechanism: A handful of buyers place most of the orders, so one of them slowing down or switching to its own chips removes a large slice of revenue at once.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast the biggest buyers shift work onto chips they design in-house.
entries.statement: NVIDIA's data-center revenue is increasingly concentrated in a few direct customers, raising demand-durability risk if any single hyperscaler slows orders or shifts to in-house silicon.
entries.title: Customer concentration risk

entries.falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within two quarters.
entries.mechanism: Selling the switches and the accelerators as one system means a buyer who swaps chip vendors must also rewire the cluster, which raises the cost of leaving.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to open rack-scale standards work that would let rival accelerators reuse the same wiring.
entries.statement: NVIDIA now leads the data-center Ethernet switch market and sells that networking bundled with its GPUs, deepening a full-system moat that raises switching costs versus standalone accelerators and custom chips. NVIDIA took the top revenue spot in data-center Ethernet switching in Q1 2026 by pairing Spectrum-X and Quantum with Blackwell and GB300, and its NVLink systems cut cost per token, but no finding compares networking growth against compute growth, so the sharper claim that networking scales faster than compute is not supported.
entries.title: Networking attach as systems moat

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
entries.mechanism: When each answer costs less to produce, workloads that were too expensive become worth running, so total chip hours rise even as the price per answer falls.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to rivals matching cost per token, since the pull-in effect helps whoever is cheapest rather than NVIDIA specifically.
entries.statement: NVIDIA's each-generation drop in cost per token pulls more inference workloads onto its GPUs and widens the market it can serve.
entries.title: Cheaper inference pulls in demand

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
entries.mechanism: Buyers who put cash down years ahead and cannot cancel have already paid for the memory, so they have strong reason to build the servers that use it.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether a buyer would rather forfeit deposits than take delivery if its own demand disappoints.
entries.statement: Non-cancelable multi-year HBM contracts backed by billions in customer deposits lock a large share of future accelerator demand into place and reduce the chance that today's buildout is speculative.
entries.title: Prepaid HBM take-or-pay locks in accelerator demand

entries.falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within two quarters.
entries.mechanism: Licences let a limited set of buyers purchase older parts under a volume ceiling, so China sales can restart but cannot return to their former size.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the volume cap or the tariff moves, since either alone decides how much can ship.
entries.statement: China datacenter compute is reopening to NVIDIA only through case-by-case H200- and MI325-class licenses capped under half of comparable US sales, with Chinese buyers now signaling first purchases. This cycle adds H200-class licensing shifted from denial to case-by-case and buyer interest from Alibaba, ByteDance and DeepSeek, broadening the earlier MI325-only picture, while China revenue sits at $4,550M and H200 licenses have booked no revenue yet.
entries.title: Conditional China re-opening with a capped ceiling

entries.falsifiableTrigger: AMD or non-NVIDIA designWins in production inference keep expanding for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: As rival software gets close enough to run the same production workloads, the cost of moving falls and price and availability start to decide the purchase.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the announced gigawatt commitments turn into working production clusters rather than pilots.
entries.statement: The difficulty of running existing AI software on non-Nvidia chips keeps customers on Nvidia even when rivals cut hardware prices.
entries.title: CUDA software lock-in sustains the moat

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within two quarters.
entries.mechanism: Memory and storage are a large part of an AI server's bill of materials, so their price rises lift the cost of every rack a buyer installs.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to when new memory fabrication capacity actually starts shipping bits.
entries.statement: Fast-rising memory and NVMe prices are pushing up what it costs to build each AI server, which could strain buyer budgets and squeeze system margins.
entries.title: Rising memory costs inflate AI-server economics

entries.falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
entries.mechanism: Four vendors hitting production in the same half adds accelerator units to the market at the same time rather than in sequence.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to shared inputs, since all four ramps draw on the same packaging and stacked-memory supply.
entries.statement: A simultaneous mass-production ramp of NVIDIA, AMD, AWS, and Google accelerators is set to expand total accelerator supply in the second half of 2026.
entries.title: Multi-vendor accelerator supply wave in second-half 2026

entries.falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next two quarters.
entries.mechanism: A handful of gigawatt-scale agreements carry nearly all the growth, so one partner delaying or cancelling moves AMD's whole accelerator line.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to the financing health of the model builders behind the largest commitments.
entries.statement: AMD's data-center accelerator growth depends on a small set of very large commitments, which concentrates both its upside and its downside in a handful of partners.
entries.title: AMD growth leans on a few mega-deals

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
entries.mechanism: Using ordinary memory on a simpler package lets a chip ship without a slot in the packaging and stacked-memory queue that limits everyone else.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the cheaper memory delivers enough speed for real inference work at scale.
entries.statement: Intel's Crescent Island inference GPU uses standard LPDDR5X memory instead of high-bandwidth memory to sidestep the advanced-packaging and memory bottleneck, opening an alternative supply route for inference chips.
entries.title: Memory-based inference chips route around the packaging bottleneck

entries.falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for two consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
entries.mechanism: When many different chip types compete for the same lines at once, the foundry can fill every node and charge more for a slot.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to a broad cut in AI capital spending, which would empty several node queues at the same time.
entries.statement: AI demand spreading across GPUs, custom ASICs, networking and power chips fills TSMC's capacity across nodes and lets it raise prices.
entries.title: Broadening AI demand tightens TSMC capacity and pricing

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within two quarters.
entries.mechanism: Spending grows faster than the cash the same businesses throw off, so the buildout depends on investors staying willing to fund it.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to cloud revenue growth holding up, since a single soft quarter would turn the spending into a visible loss.
entries.statement: Hyperscalers' sharp jump in AI capital spending risks a pullback if returns disappoint, which would cut accelerator orders.
entries.title: Hyperscaler AI spending may outrun near-term returns

entries.falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
entries.mechanism: Buyers accept the asking price because supply is short and no rival ships an equivalent system in volume, so cost increases pass through.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory contract prices, which are forecast to roughly double into 2027 and sit inside the bill of materials.
entries.statement: NVIDIA keeps its gross margin near three-quarters even while ramping new products, far above rivals, showing buyers still pay premium prices.
entries.title: NVIDIA holds a premium gross margin as it ramps new chips

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
entries.mechanism: A handful of customers book nearly all the packaging line, so the supplier's utilisation depends on those same few order books staying full.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether custom-chip and networking customers grow large enough to backfill a lost GPU booking.
entries.statement: A few AI chip buyers control most of TSMC's advanced-packaging output, so any one of them cutting orders would leave capacity that is hard to refill.
entries.title: AI packaging supply is concentrated in a few buyers

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over two quarters.
entries.mechanism: Buyers who fear being short of compute sign longer contracts to hold a place in the queue, which pushes the average life of the order book further out.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to supply loosening, since buyers stop pre-booking years ahead once parts are available on demand.
entries.statement: Cloud and chip suppliers are signing longer-dated purchase commitments that push out the average life of their order books, so a growing share of AI compute demand is booked years in advance.
entries.title: Backlog duration lengthens as demand is booked years ahead

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
entries.mechanism: Model providers pay for compute out of paying customers rather than only out of investment money, so their orders rest on sales that already exist.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much of that revenue is itself funded by chip vendors taking equity in the same model providers.
entries.statement: Leading AI model providers are growing revenue fast enough that their heavy compute spending rests on real and rising sales rather than hope.
entries.title: Model-provider revenue scales to underpin the buildout

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next two quarters.
entries.mechanism: With the best foreign parts blocked, Chinese buyers move spending to home-grown accelerators, which lifts those suppliers' sales even where performance still lags.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether domestic supply can grow fast enough to cover the roughly two million units of unmet demand.
entries.statement: China's home-grown accelerators can now train frontier-scale models without NVIDIA chips, but Chinese buyers still order far more NVIDIA parts than are available, so the displacement is proven in capability and not yet in volume. Two findings show a 1.6-trillion-parameter model pretrained on more than 50,000 domestic accelerators across over 35 trillion tokens, while Chinese firms ordered more than two million restricted NVIDIA parts for 2026 against roughly 700,000 units of inventory and domestic labs' own chips are judged more than two years away.
entries.title: China Domestic Accelerators Displace Banned NVIDIA GPUs

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Buying fleets on debt puts interest and depreciation on the books before the rental income arrives, so faster growth deepens the loss.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to rental prices holding, since the loans were sized against today's hourly rates.
entries.statement: Fast-growing neocloud GPU buyers such as CoreWeave are booking record revenue while their net losses widen.
entries.title: Neocloud GPU Buyers Grow Revenue but Deepen Losses

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
entries.mechanism: A site can only run as many racks as it has electricity and grid gear for, so power decides deployment once chips are available.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to grid equipment lead times, which are far longer than chip lead times.
entries.statement: Companies now size and cap their AI buildouts by gigawatts of available power, so electricity and site capacity increasingly limit how many accelerators they can actually deploy.
entries.title: Power capacity is becoming the binding limit on AI buildout

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
entries.mechanism: Designing a competitive accelerator needs skills only a couple of firms sell, so the escape route from merchant GPUs runs through the same two suppliers.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether new entrants such as memory makers turn early talks into shipping designs.
entries.statement: Hyperscalers' shift to custom AI chips runs almost entirely through two outside design firms, so the alternative to merchant GPUs is itself concentrated in those two suppliers.
entries.title: The custom-AI-chip alternative depends on two design houses

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for two consecutive months.
entries.mechanism: Contract manufacturers only book revenue when finished servers leave the factory, so their monthly sales show real deliveries rather than orders.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory and packaging shortfalls, which stall finished-system assembly even with orders in hand.
entries.statement: Contract server makers post record monthly revenue as AI-server and networking orders ship in volume.
entries.title: ODM AI-server revenue confirms real shipments

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within two quarters.
entries.mechanism: Fleets bought with borrowed money leave a small equity cushion, so a drop in rental income quickly threatens the loan payments.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to interest costs and to the vendor guarantees that currently backstop unused capacity.
entries.statement: Neocloud operators fund their GPU fleets mostly with debt, leaving thin equity cushions.
entries.title: Neocloud GPU buyers carry heavy debt loads

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
entries.mechanism: Putting the optics inside the switch package saves power and cuts parts, which moves cluster wiring onto a different and faster-moving supply chain.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to packaging yield, since the new optics compete for the same advanced-packaging capacity as accelerators.
entries.statement: The move to co-packaged optics is reshaping how AI networking gear is built and supplied, tying cluster wiring to a fast-changing optics roadmap.
entries.title: Optical networking shifts to co-packaged optics as a supply lever

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
entries.mechanism: Committed money and started construction move some fabrication and assembly outside Taiwan, which spreads where the same parts can be made.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to construction and grid timelines, since announced money says nothing about when output starts.
entries.statement: NVIDIA and its partners are committing to build AI hardware inside the United States at very large scale, adding fabrication and packaging capacity outside Taiwan.
entries.title: US onshoring broadens the AI hardware supply base

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Providers cannot build capacity fast enough to serve signed contracts, so revenue measures their delivery rate while the backlog measures demand.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to contract quality, since backlog counts commitments from customers who may themselves be vendor-funded.
entries.statement: Cloud providers are booking compute contracts far faster than they can deliver them, so their reported backlogs now show demand better than their quarterly sales do.
entries.title: Cloud backlog conversion becomes the demand proof point

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Capital spending now exceeds the cash these businesses generate, so the shortfall is covered by issuing debt and shares.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to credit and equity market appetite, which sets how long spending can outrun cash flow.
entries.statement: The largest cloud buyers are turning to debt and share issuance to pay for AI capacity instead of funding it from cash generated by their businesses.
entries.title: Hyperscalers now borrow to fund the buildout

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
entries.mechanism: More work per megawatt means a site with fixed electricity can serve more workloads without adding racks, which softens the power and packaging ceiling.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether vendor efficiency claims hold up in independent measurement, which has so far come in lower.
entries.statement: Each new generation of AI racks does far more work per megawatt, which lets buyers add capacity even when power and packaging are capped.
entries.title: Efficiency gains stretch scarce power and packaging

entries.falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for two consecutive quarters before end-2027.
entries.mechanism: Each accelerator needs a fixed stack of memory, so the number of memory stacks a supplier can build sets the number of accelerators that can ship.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to yield on the next memory generation, which uses three times the wafer capacity of standard parts.
entries.statement: Stacked memory, not chips or packaging alone, now decides how many accelerators NVIDIA and AMD can actually deliver.
entries.title: Memory supply is the new choke point on accelerator shipments

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier gross margin falls for two consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.
entries.mechanism: Because memory is the scarcest part in the server, its makers set the price and take a bigger slice of what the finished system earns.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory capacity, since the margin rests entirely on scarcity rather than on a technology lead.
entries.statement: Memory suppliers are earning extraordinary margins on AI parts, shifting profit from the server builders toward the memory makers.
entries.title: Memory makers capture a growing share of AI server profit

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 GPUs is announced for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Governments and large companies now buy clusters big enough to compete for the same scarce parts as the cloud giants, which widens the buyer base.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to national budgets and power availability at the chosen sites.
entries.statement: National projects and large enterprises are now placing accelerator orders big enough to matter alongside the cloud giants.
entries.title: Sovereign and enterprise buyers become a new demand tier

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Intel data-center revenue growth falls below 10% year over year for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Better factory yields and outside foundry customers let Intel sell both its own server parts and manufacturing capacity, adding a third source of supply.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the first external foundry customers grow into volume, since the announced deals carry no disclosed size.
entries.statement: Intel's data-center and foundry businesses are growing again with better margins, adding a third source of AI-adjacent supply.
entries.title: Intel returns as a data-center supplier

entries.falsifiableTrigger: New vendor equity-for-compute deals in marginalBuyerFinancing stop appearing for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: When the chip seller owns part of the buyer, some of the money paid for chips originally came from the seller, so reported demand partly reflects its own investment.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the funded customers reach revenue that covers their compute bills on their own.
entries.statement: Merchant accelerator vendors are now buying equity stakes in the AI firms that buy their chips, tying reported demand to vendor-funded customers beyond NVIDIA alone.
entries.title: chipmakers take equity in their own customers

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Standard DRAM S10 spot prices fall for two consecutive months as suppliers restore non-AI capacity.
entries.mechanism: Memory makers move production lines to the higher-priced AI parts, which leaves less standard memory and lifts prices on everyday products.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to when new fabrication capacity comes online, which suppliers place no earlier than late 2026.
entries.statement: The stacked-memory shortage is spreading into standard memory and raising prices on consumer and general-purpose graphics parts.
entries.title: memory crunch spills into consumer and general-purpose parts

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No new multi-year accelerator-to-memory supply partnership is announced for two consecutive quarters through 2027.
entries.mechanism: With memory the scarcest input, accelerator makers contract straight with the memory suppliers to reserve output rather than compete for it later on the open market.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory supply loosening, which would remove the reason to lock output years ahead.
entries.statement: Accelerator makers are signing multi-year partnerships and joint development deals straight with memory suppliers to reserve future stacked-memory output.
entries.title: Chip vendors buy their memory supply directly

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The leading supplier's HBM market-share-pct falls below 50% within four quarters as rivals ship volume.
entries.mechanism: One supplier makes most of the memory that accelerators need and its output is pre-sold to the largest buyers, so smaller buyers cannot get parts at any price.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to rival yields on the next memory generation, since qualification is what actually shifts share.
entries.statement: One supplier holds most of the stacked-memory market and the largest cloud buyers have locked up long-term contracts, so access to that single source now decides who can build AI servers.
entries.title: Stacked-memory supply sits with one dominant maker

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No new diversion prosecution or whitelist reduction is reported for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Prosecutions and a shorter approved-buyer list raise the personal and commercial cost of reselling restricted parts, which shuts the informal channels.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to the size of the price gap between licensed and unlicensed supply, which sets how much smuggling pays.
entries.statement: Criminal investigations and tighter buyer whitelists are shutting the informal channels that moved restricted AI chips into China.
entries.title: Enforcement closes the gray route into China

entries.falsifiableTrigger: CoWoS lead times stay above 52 weeks through the end of 2027 while the supply gap fails to narrow below 15%.
entries.mechanism: Packaging capacity can be added by building more lines and hiring outside assembly partners, while memory needs new fabs and better yields, so the two constraints loosen on different clocks.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether outside assembly partners can qualify at the same quality as the lead supplier.
entries.statement: The advanced-packaging shortage is set to narrow over the next year as capacity expands and outside assembly partners join in, leaving memory as the tighter of the two limits on accelerator output.
entries.title: Packaging tightness starts to ease while memory does not

entries.falsifiableTrigger: NAND contract prices for server drives fall for two consecutive quarters while Rubin deployments keep growing.
entries.mechanism: A new hardware tier that needs hundreds of drives per unit adds demand for flash faster than makers can add lines, so its price and lead time climb like memory's did.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly Rubin-generation racks actually deploy, since the demand step depends on that ramp.
entries.statement: The newest accelerator generation adds a large storage tier that is pulling flash demand up sharply and is already showing up as rising server costs.
entries.title: Storage becomes the next scarce part in the AI rack

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Public list rates for the newest rack-scale systems appear on major provider pricing pages within two quarters.
entries.mechanism: When the newest hardware is scarce, providers hold back list prices and negotiate each contract, which keeps the highest prices out of public view.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to supply loosening, since providers publish rates again once they need to fill idle capacity.
entries.statement: Cloud providers publish rates for last-generation accelerators but quote their newest systems only through sales, so listed prices no longer show what the leading edge costs.
entries.title: The newest systems leave the public price list
